title: `EditorPlugin.remove_autoload_singleton()` no longer removes the autoload from project settings
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.8.dev7 [c971f93e7], 4.8.dev1 [ebbf577a0] (dev2-dev6 not tested).
- Not reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable [ed1daf0bf].
- Not tested in current `master` [e7cfa294a], but the code involved is unchanged there since 4.8.dev7.

### System information

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Linux 6.18, x86_64), Intel Xeon @ 2.80GHz (4 threads) - official Linux x86_64 builds, editor run with `--headless --editor` (no GPU). Only tested on Linux.

### Issue description

A plugin that calls `add_autoload_singleton()` in `_enable_plugin()` and `remove_autoload_singleton()` in `_disable_plugin()` no longer gets rid of its autoload when it is disabled. After disabling the plugin in 4.8:

- `ProjectSettings.has_setting("autoload/ReproAutoload")` is still `true`;
- the autoload is still listed in Project Settings > Globals > Autoload;
- `project.godot` still has it under `[autoload]`, and it is still there after an editor restart;
- running the project still instantiates the autoload (`ReproAutoload is running` is printed).

In 4.7.2.stable the same steps remove the setting, the `project.godot` entry and the autoload at runtime.

From reading the source (links to `master` e7cfa294a):

- `EditorPlugin::remove_autoload_singleton()` calls `EditorAutoloadSettings::autoload_remove()` ([editor_plugin.cpp#L85-L87](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/editor/plugins/editor_plugin.cpp#L85-L87)). That now only calls `ProjectSettings::remove_autoload()` ([editor_autoload_settings.cpp#L827-L831](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/editor/settings/editor_autoload_settings.cpp#L827-L831)). `ProjectSettings::remove_autoload()` erases the entry from the in-memory `autoloads` map but leaves the `autoload/<name>` property in place ([project_settings.cpp#L1518-L1521](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/core/config/project_settings.cpp#L1518-L1521)). `update_autoload()` then rebuilds the list from the `autoload/*` properties ([editor_autoload_settings.cpp#L487-L491](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/editor/settings/editor_autoload_settings.cpp#L487-L491)), and the next save writes the property to `project.godot`.
- On the add side, `autoload_add(..., false)` (the path used by `add_autoload_singleton()`) does write the property with `ProjectSettings::set()` ([editor_autoload_settings.cpp#L797-L802](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/editor/settings/editor_autoload_settings.cpp#L797-L802)).
- In 4.7.2, `autoload_remove()` set the property to `Variant()` through an undo/redo action ([4.7.2-stable editor_autoload_settings.cpp#L806-L827](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/editor/settings/editor_autoload_settings.cpp#L806-L827)), which erased both the property and the map entry ([project_settings.cpp#L303-L308](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/core/config/project_settings.cpp#L303-L308), unchanged since 4.7.2).
- `autoload_remove()` was changed in #109863 (commit a966a2a965). It is the only commit that touches this function between `4.7-stable` and `master` (`git log -L`). Its description says it makes `add/remove_autoload_singleton()` "no longer create undo action".

Is it intended that `remove_autoload_singleton()` now leaves the `autoload/<name>` setting in place?

The Delete button in the Autoload tab uses its own undo/redo action ([editor_autoload_settings.cpp#L298-L315](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e7cfa294a0b81bed7986be04a848cc1832a3f083/editor/settings/editor_autoload_settings.cpp#L298-L315)) and does not seem to be affected. I only checked that by reading the code.

Workaround in plugin code (tested on 4.8.dev7): call `ProjectSettings.set_setting("autoload/" + name, null)` after `remove_autoload_singleton()`. This removes the setting and the `project.godot` entry, but the Autoload tab keeps showing the entry until it is refreshed.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the MRP. The plugin "Autoload Repro" is disabled and `project.godot` has no `[autoload]` section.
2. Project > Project Settings > Plugins: enable "Autoload Repro". Globals > Autoload now lists `ReproAutoload`, and `project.godot` gets `ReproAutoload="*res://addons/autoload_repro/repro_autoload.gd"`.
3. Disable "Autoload Repro".
4. Check Globals > Autoload and, after a couple of seconds, `project.godot`.
5. Restart the editor and run the project.

Expected (4.7.2 behavior): after step 3 the autoload is gone from the Autoload tab, from `ProjectSettings` and from `project.godot`, and running the project prints nothing.

Actual (4.8.dev1, 4.8.dev7): the autoload stays in all three places, and running the project prints `ReproAutoload is running`.

I ran these steps from a small editor script in a headless editor rather than by clicking. It toggles the plugin with `EditorInterface.set_plugin_enabled()`, which goes through the same `EditorNode::set_addon_plugin_enabled(name, enabled, true)` as the Plugins tab checkbox, and then reads `ProjectSettings` and `project.godot`.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

The project is three small files plus an empty main scene, so here it is in full instead of a zip. Create an empty project and add:

`addons/autoload_repro/plugin.cfg`:

```ini
[plugin]

name="Autoload Repro"
description="Adds an autoload in _enable_plugin() and removes it in _disable_plugin()."
author="godot-mcp"
version="1.0"
script="plugin.gd"
```

`addons/autoload_repro/plugin.gd`:

```gdscript
@tool
extends EditorPlugin

const AUTOLOAD_NAME := "ReproAutoload"
const AUTOLOAD_PATH := "res://addons/autoload_repro/repro_autoload.gd"


func _enable_plugin() -> void:
	add_autoload_singleton(AUTOLOAD_NAME, AUTOLOAD_PATH)


func _disable_plugin() -> void:
	remove_autoload_singleton(AUTOLOAD_NAME)
```

`addons/autoload_repro/repro_autoload.gd`:

```gdscript
extends Node


func _ready() -> void:
	print("ReproAutoload is running")
```

`main.tscn` is a single `Node` set as the main scene. I can attach the project as a zip if that is more convenient.

---

*Disclosure: this was found by running an editor plugin's integration test suite against 4.8.dev7. The analysis and this report were prepared with the help of an AI coding assistant (Claude); the reproduction above was actually run on the listed builds, and the source references were checked against the linked commits.*
